items.title: EW 30 onder 30
items.subtitle: Named one of EW Magazine’s thirty young talents under thirty.
items.text: Recognised for combining medicine, anthropology and evolutionary science in her research on iodine, the thyroid and child development.
items.quote: Schildklierproblemen komen vaker voor bij vrouwen en we snappen niet precies waarom. […] Tijd om daar verandering in te brengen.
items.quoteTranslation: Thyroid problems are more common in women, and we don’t understand exactly why. […] Time to change that.
items.imageAlt: Sarai Keestra in a garden, holding a white coat and a stethoscope

items.title: Graduated as a medical doctor
items.text: Finished medical school at Amsterdam UMC in May 2026. The PhD on iodine and thyroid health in the first thousand days continues.

items.title: School-age development after an X-ray fertility test with iodine-containing contrast
items.text: In the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism: children conceived within six months of hysterosalpingography, an X-ray fertility test using iodine-containing contrast to check whether the fallopian tubes are open, had lower average IQ scores and lower scores for information processing and attention control than children conceived without fertility treatment. No differences were found in behaviour or school performance. This small observational study cannot establish causation, and the authors call for replication in larger cohorts.
